title: The Matrix
synopsis: Wake up, Neo. The white rabbit, the office, the call. Red pill, blue pill. Choose what kind of life you were going to have anyway.

nodes.text: A green prompt. Wake up, Neo. A knock at the door. Choi will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Open” than after “Pretend not to be home.” At Choi, the decision will matter as data as well as intent.

choices.consequence: You commit to open. It carries you toward Choi, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You pretend not to be home. The path to Choi opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Two grand for the disk. Follow the white rabbit, he says. Trinity comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Go with them” and “Stay home.” At Trinity, the decision will matter as data as well as intent.

choices.consequence: You commit to go with them. It carries you toward Trinity, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You commit to stay home. It carries you toward Trinity, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: A woman in leather at a club. She tells you the question is what drives you. The road still runs toward The Office. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Listen” and choosing “Stay alert.”

choices.consequence: You listen. The path to The Office opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You commit to stay alert. It carries you toward The Office, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Agents at your desk. Smith. Phone in a parcel. Both choices lead to Window Ledge, but “Take the phone” arrives there with a different cost than “Go with the agents.” In The Office, the rules change the moment you decide they can be tested.

choices.consequence: You choose to take the phone. By Window Ledge, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You choose to go with the agents. By Window Ledge, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: Morpheus says go to the ledge. You can't. They take you. You cannot avoid Bug; you can only decide whether “Try anyway” or “Cooperate” defines the person who reaches it. In Window Ledge, the rules change the moment you decide they can be tested.

choices.consequence: You choose to try anyway. By Bug, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: Call ended. You step out of the booth. You can fly. “Fly” opens the route to The One. “Walk a block first” changes the terms and carries you toward Zion's Builder. A third choice, “Take the third path,” keeps Peace with the Machines in play.

choices.consequence: You fly. The path to The One opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You choose to walk a block first. By Zion's Builder, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
Some endings reveal themselves last. You commit to take the third path. It carries you toward Peace with the Machines, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: You become a teacher and a target. You fly often. You also, occasionally, take the bus, because the bus passes a place that used to be your apartment. The road into The One began with “Fly” in Phone Booth; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You spend a decade rebuilding Zion's defenses. You marry Trinity. You retire, eventually, to teach kids how to fly. The kids, mostly, prefer running. The road into Zion's Builder began with “Walk a block first” in Phone Booth; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You broker, eventually, a peace between humans and machines. The truce holds for a generation. After that, you don't know. You are, for now, content with a generation. The road into Peace with the Machines began with “Take the third path” in Phone Booth; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.
